issues.body: The prior finding remains unchanged at `_apt_packages_in_line`: `[[ $cmd_pos -eq 1 && "$tok" == ?*=* ]] && continue` tests the raw token without establishing that the assignment word is unquoted. For `RUN "FOO=bar" apt-get install -y jq python3-yaml`, the token has an even quote count, is accepted as an assignment prefix, and leaves `cmd_pos=1`; the parser then counts both packages. The shell instead treats the quoted first word as the command name `FOO=bar`, so apt-get is never reached. `_assert_container_selftest_deps` consequently returns success for an image that installs neither dependency. The newly added tests do not include this quoted assignment-shaped command-word case.
issues.fix_hint: Recognize assignment prefixes according to shell quoting semantics, declining to count packages whenever that classification is uncertain. Add a regression fixture through `_assert_container_selftest_deps` using a quoted assignment-shaped command word and expect `missing`, plus retain an unquoted `FOO=bar apt-get ...` positive control expecting `satisfied`.
issues.title: Quoted assignment-shaped command words still fabricate installed packages

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 5 leaves the prior major fail-open finding unresolved. The assignment-prefix arm still classifies a raw, quoted assignment-shaped command word as a shell assignment, and there is still no regression fixture covering that case. The dependency gate can therefore report both required packages as provisioned even though the shell never executes apt-get. Progress is stagnant because the same major issue remains at the same severity.
